result.html:
The end-state is exactly right. Confirmed visually:

- **Gate OPEN**: shutters retracted, the green mint seam glows down the center, the merged mint particle st
result.winner_angle: A living directed-acyclic-graph rendered as a vertical 'data foundry' pipeline: prompt -> script -> 5-wide fan-out -> a physical BARRIER GATE -> synthesize -> r
result.winner_rationale: Concept A wins because it scores highest on the two heaviest criteria (accuracy potential and pedagogy) without sacrificing the other three. PEDAGOGY: it is the

ranking.angle: A living directed-acyclic-graph rendered as a vertical 'data foundry' pipeline: prompt -> script -> 5-wide fan-out -> a physical BARRIER GATE -> synthesize -> result, as a deterministic scrubbable replay of the real 6.0-minute run.
ranking.strengths: Best overall balance of all five criteria. Triple-encodes the fan-out->barrier->reduce shape simultaneously in geometry (1 trunk -> 5 lanes -> 1 spillway), color (5 hues blending to 1 mint), and time (5 simultaneous launches, a held gate, one merged release) so the core concept lands even without reading. The physical gate that visibly REFUSES to open at 3/5 and 4/5 is the most visceral, watchable teaching of 'parallel() waits for ALL' of any concept. Faithful to the real run: exact 6-node DAG, all 5 real angle labels, both log() lines, scrubbable deterministic replay mapped to 360,818 ms, journaled-resume demo, context-window boundary callout. Graphite+single-signal-teal palette is premium and avoids AI-slop. getPointAtLength particle-on-path motion is literal data-in-motion, not vague glow. Richest correct interactivity (scrub, hover-isolate, script unfold, resume toast, reduced-motion fallback).
ranking.weaknesses: Hardcodes 'Collected 23 sourced findings' and a totalFindings tile of 23 -- the real run is 67 (trivial one-string fix, but currently wrong). The 6-cell FINDINGS_SCHEMA validation strip implies per-finding fields {claim, source_url, source_title, published} that are NOT in the actual return (return only has {angle, found, summary}); rendering them as 'validated' overstates what the run produced. Highest single-file build complexity and perf risk: many SVG conduits each running particle systems + scrub-reversible CSS state across 6 bands in a tall 1200x1640 portrait canvas -- the most places for bugs and jank on weak machines.

ranking.angle: EXECUTION TIMELINE / SWIMLANE (Gantt-like observability dashboard) whose single job is to make the parallel() BARRIER undeniable via a welded Synthesize bar edge, a staged reveal, and an in-flight concurrency strip.
ranking.strengths: Most accuracy-robust and screenshot-proof concept: the barrier is encoded THREE independent ways that all survive a static screenshot -- the Synthesize bar's left edge geometrically welded to the amber barrier line, the staged intro that makes you WAIT for Synthesize, and the in-flight step-strip dropping to 0 before the synth blip. Canonical, instantly credible engineer form (distributed-trace waterfall) re-skinned as an instrument board so it dodges the rounded-purple-card cliche. The concurrency gutter -- peak-of-5 plotted far below a dashed 'cap = 16' ceiling with the 11 idle slots explicitly shaded -- is a uniquely truthful insight no other concept surfaces. Cites the finding count generically ('N findings', 'Collected N across 5/5'), so it does not fabricate the total. Lowest build/perf risk after C: inline SVG bars/grid/barrier + vanilla count-ups + one playhead.
ranking.weaknesses: Lower originality and 'wow' than A and C -- a swimlane is the expected shape, so it impresses less on first glance. Teaches the two subtler ideas more weakly than rivals: 'the script is code Claude wrote' and 'intermediate results stay out of Claude's context' live only as bottom-strip prose callouts, not as spatial drama. The 'water-behind-a-dam' fill metaphor is nice but secondary. Per-bar tool-tick notches 'summing to 85' is an invented per-agent split (the run gives only the 85 total), a minor fabrication if read literally.

ranking.angle: SCRIPT <-> RUNTIME: a two-pane annotated engineering blueprint where the left pane is the JS source Claude wrote and the right pane is the live execution graph, with cursor-fired signal beams in the gutter mapping code lines to runtime nodes.
ranking.strengths: Best pedagogy of the single hardest leap -- code -> runtime. Hovering the parallel(...) line firing five beams to five lanes, and the synthesize line firing five beams INTO one node, turns 'this abstraction becomes that execution' from a claim into something you trigger with your cursor; bidirectional, pinnable, keyboard-navigable. Best treatment of the context-window concept of any concept: a dashed boundary with exactly ONE crossing wire (the return) plus a spotlight button, with purple used exactly once so it carries meaning. The most disciplined, original art direction (drafting/ozalid palette, one cyan signature, one amber convergence, one red stop-bar, Menlo throughout) -- reads like a pinned engineering sheet, the furthest from generic. Shows the real primitives as source and the real run tolerances on a dimension line. The barrier-vs-pipeline toggle on the red bus-bar lets the viewer A/B the concept in one second. Honestly flags that the script API is community-reverse-engineered, not official.
ranking.weaknesses: Two dense panes + a beam-routing gutter is a fair amount of SVG/layout work and the left code pane must show plausible-but-not-officially-specified source. Less 'watchable' continuous motion than the two player concepts -- the payoff is interaction-driven, so a passive viewer or a screenshot gets less of the dynamism. Expanding lane cards to show example findings rows {claim, source_title, published} risks showing illustrative data the real return does not contain (mitigated by being opt-in and labeled as examples).

ranking.angle: Run Console -- an interactive replay PLAYER: a transport bar drives a 12-keyframe timeline; left a live log() console, right a 6-lane agent rack with a physical shutter barrier, plus a narration caption that teaches each beat.
ranking.strengths: Best transport UX and the most explicitly pedagogical framing of time: play/pause/step/scrub over 12 deterministic keyframes that reverse exactly, so a learner can freeze on the frame the barrier closes and read WHY Synthesize waits, then scrub back to watch an agent auto-retry -- and the reversible player itself embodies the run's journaled/resumable nature. The context gutter (green finding-packets sealed into a 'script variables (not in context)' canister while exactly ONE gold return packet escapes upward to 'conversation') is an excellent one-glance teaching of the feature's whole point. Calm phosphor-green/amber/emerald instrument palette with cyan reserved for the single synthesize agent and gold for the return is disciplined and slop-free. Honestly buildable (rAF over a keyframe array, inline SVG rack/shutter, CSS card flip).
ranking.weaknesses: Worst accuracy liabilities as specified: hardcodes totalFindings:18, invents a per-angle found-count breakdown (4,3,5,2,4), and shows per-agent findings drawers with {claim, source_title, published} that do NOT exist in the real return ({angle, found, summary} only) -- a viewer would screenshot fabricated numbers and rows. Real total is 67. The shutter-across-the-rack barrier metaphor overlaps heavily with Concept A's gate, so it is less original in a field that already contains A. The single-stage 'spotlight' framing shows less of the whole DAG topology at once than A/B/C.

graft_elements: Correct the data first (from the verified run output ww22q8os9.output): totalFindings = 67 (not 23/18); second log line verbatim = 'Collected 67 sourced findings across 5/5 angles.'; first log line verbatim = 'Fanning out 5 web-research agents on distinct angles of Claude Code Dynamic Workflows…'; per-angle objects are {angle, found, summary} ONLY -- there is no nested findings[] array, no per-angle counts, and no {claim, source_url, source_title, published} rows in the return. Drive any hover detail from the real summary text, and label any per-finding/claim UI explicitly as illustrative if shown at all.

From Concept B (timeline): weld the Synthesize node's start to the barrier the way B welds the Synthesize bar's left edge to the amber barrier line, and stage the reveal so Synthesize literally cannot appear until the gate opens -- this makes A's barrier survive a STATIC screenshot, not just the animation, covering A's main weakness (it otherwise only proves the barrier while playing).

From Concept B (timeline): add the truth-telling concurrency strip -- a small step plot of in-flight agents that peaks at 5 against a dashed 'cap = 16' ceiling with the '11 slots idle' gap shaded, plus '1000/run hard cap' fine print. This is a unique, non-junk insight A lacks and it ties the abstract concurrency cap to a concrete mark.

From Concept B (timeline): include the explicit 'parallel <-> pipeline (HYPOTHETICAL)' A/B toggle (clearly labeled hypothetical) so the viewer can see how pipeline() would stream Synthesize per item with no single barrier -- teaches the parallel-vs-pipeline distinction the actual run does not itself show.

From Concept C (blueprint): add the bidirectional, cursor-fired code<->runtime mapping -- a collapsible 'script.js' source panel where hovering the parallel(...map(agent{schema})) line fires beams to all 5 lanes + the gate, and hovering the synthesize line fires beams from all 5 into the one node. A already has a click-to-unfold script node; upgrade it to C's hover-beam mapping so the code->runtime leap is demonstrated, not just listed. Honestly note the script API is community-reverse-engineered, not official.

From Concept C (blueprint): adopt C's emphatic context-window treatment as A's signature teaching moment -- a dashed 'conversation context' boundary at the bottom with everything above shaded 'script variables (308,221 tokens, never enter Claude's context)' and exactly ONE thin wire (the return {synthesis, angleSummaries, totalFindings}) crossing it, plus a spotlight button that fades everything else. Reserve a single accent color for that boundary so it reads as meaning, not decoration.

From Concept D (player): adopt the full transport control surface -- play/pause/step-back/step-forward, a notched keyframe scrub track with mm:ss out of 6:01, and 0.5x/1x/2x speed -- driven by a precomputed keyframe array so scrubbing BACKWARD reverses every state exactly (re-latches the gate, un-types logs, hides the result). A already wants a scrubbable replay; D's keyframe-array approach is the cleanest way to guarantee determinism and reversibility and to embody the journaled/resumable story.

From Concept D (player): add the live log() console echoing the two real log lines as they fire (typing with a caret, active-line accent), paired to the timeline. It anchors each animation beat to a verbatim runtime fact and reinforces 'Fanning out 5…' at fan-out and 'Collected 67…' at gate-open.

From Concept D (player): add the per-beat narration caption with an info popover that surfaces the right teaching fact at the right moment (barrier semantics at the gate; failed-thunk->null/.filter(Boolean) when a lane could fail; 16-concurrent/1000-cap; journaled & resumable) -- turns A's static side callouts into time-synced, just-in-time pedagogy.

Universal robustness/accessibility floor from B/C/D: keep everything as inline SVG + one rAF clock + CSS transitions on data-state attributes with NO external requests; honor prefers-reduced-motion (freeze particles to static dashed flow, cross-fade the gate red->green instead of sliding, show full typed text instantly); use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every animating counter; and keep the provenance footer exact: research-claude-dynamic-workflows, released 2026-05-28, research preview, Claude Code v2.1.154, Claude Opus 4.8.

logs: Generating 4 independent visualization concepts in parallel…

Got 4 concepts: A living directed-acyclic-graph rendered as a vertical "data foundry" pipeline: prompt → script → 5-wide fan-out → a physical BARRIER GATE → synthesize → result. The whole piece is a single inline-SVG circuit board where edges are literal conduits carrying glowing particle packets, and the barrier is a real gate that stays SHUT (red) until all 5 lanes deposit their payload, then flips OPEN (green) and releases one merged stream downward. The animation is a deterministic, scrubbable replay of the real 6.0-minute run, not a loop of vague pulses., EXECUTION TIMELINE / SWIMLANE (Gantt-like observability dashboard). Horizontal time axis 0:00 → 6:01 (360,818 ms). Each of the 6 agents is one horizontal bar in its own lane, colored by phase. The single design job of the chart is to make the parallel() BARRIER physically undeniable: the five Search bars overlap inside a shaded "Search band," their right edges fray at slightly different x-positions (real agents finish at different times), and a hard vertical "BARRIER" rule is dropped at the x of the LAST search bar's completion. The lone Synthesize bar is rendered with its left edge welded to that rule — it literally cannot begin one pixel earlier. A right-side concurrency gutter shows a live "in-flight" count that peaks at 5 against a dashed ceiling labeled "max 16," proving the run never saturated the pool., A two-pane "annotated engineering blueprint" that treats the workflow as a circuit diagram. LEFT pane = the JavaScript source Claude wrote (the schematic). RIGHT pane = the live execution graph the background runtime produced (the populated board). The teaching happens in the GUTTER between them: hovering any code line fires a literal "signal beam" across the gutter into the runtime nodes it created, so the viewer SEES that parallel([...]) on line 34 becomes five concurrent lanes, and that the single agent({}) on line 58 becomes the one Synthesize node fed by all five. The whole thing is drawn like a drafting sheet — hairline grid, corner tick marks, a title block, dimension lines with the real run stats (6 agents · 85 tools · 308,221 tokens · 6.0 min) called out like measured tolerances. It deliberately rejects the "AI product" look: no glassmorphism, no purple gradient, no glow-on-everything. It looks like something an engineer pinned to a wall., An interactive replay PLAYER, not a static diagram. A single horizontal transport bar (play / pause / step / scrub) drives a 12-keyframe timeline of one real run. The screen is a focused two-pane "spotlight": LEFT a live console echoing the actual log() lines as they're emitted, RIGHT a vertical agent-rack of 6 lanes that light up, spin, and resolve in real time. A narration caption under the transport teaches WHAT is happening and WHY at each beat. The whole thing is time-based and pedagogical: you literally watch the prompt compile, 5 agents fan out and stream, the barrier slam shut, and the synthesize agent flip the result card in. Scrubbing backward rewinds state exactly (it reads from a precomputed keyframe array, so every position is deterministic — mirroring the run's own journaled/resumable nature). One stage in the spotlight at a time; everything else recedes.

Winner: A living directed-acyclic-graph rendered as a vertical 'data foundry' pipeline: prompt -> script -> 5-wide fan-out -> a physical BARRIER GATE -> synthesize -> result, animated as a deterministic, scrubbable replay of the real 6.0-minute run (Concept A: 'BARRIER — a living DAG of one Dynamic Workflow run').. Grafting 10 elements from runners-up.
